subject: Clarify rate card + streaming metering for partial/interrupt scenarios
messages:
From: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@nebulahealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Rate card + streaming metering questions

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nebula Health is excited about Redwood's latency and cost controls. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of rate-card clarifications before we start an internal approval:

1) How are streaming responses metered when a session produces a partial generation (e.g., client disconnects after 200 of an expected 800 tokens)? Do you charge for tokens generated or for the requested budget?
2) If we retry the request (client reconnects and asks Redwood to continue) will there be double charges for the overlapping portion?
3) For transient disconnects (TCP/WS blips), do you have a grace/resume window where you don't bill the interrupted session as a full generation?

We have a preferred commit range in mind (2M tokens/month baseline) and we'd like to understand how streaming behavior will affect monthly unit economics. Can you send the baseline rate card and a short note on streaming billing edge cases?

Best,
Sam
Sam Brooks
Director, Engineering
Nebula Health
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + streaming metering questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear questions and for the time last week. Attaching our Q3 rate card and a spreadsheet with an example cost calc for a 2M token commit. Quick summary below, and I copied Marissa (pricing) and Stephanie (billing) to make sure we're clear on commercial treatment.

Short answers (high level):
- Metering: we bill tokens emitted by the model (actual output tokens). If a session disconnects after 200 tokens, you will be billed for those 200 output tokens.
- Retries: when a client reconnects and asks us to continue from the last emitted token, we do not double-bill overlapping tokens — we use explicit continuation tokens and only charge for newly emitted tokens.
- Grace window: for streaming protocol disconnects (short WS/TCP blips) we have a 90-second session resume window where we hold the KV cache and do not charge for retries within that window beyond emitted tokens. Longer interruptions will be treated as a new session.

Edge-case note: if an application-side retry resubmits the same request without a continuation token (e.g., client retries blindly), our default deduplication can prevent double charges only if the retry hits the same serving node within a short timeframe. For guaranteed dedupe across distributed retries we recommend using our idempotency token header — that ensures the platform treats retries as replays and won't re-charge for already-fulfilled output.

Attachments: Redwood-Rate-Card-Q3-2027.pdf (baseline rates and discount tiers), Nebula-Proposed-Commit-and-Discount.xlsx (sample math).

If that looks good, Marissa and I can propose a starter commercial (commit + temporary connectivity credit) to get you through PoC.

Cheers,
Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Rate card + streaming metering questions

Team — forwarding Sam's questions and my reply. Key ask from Nebula: baseline rate confirmation for 2M tokens/month and clarity on streaming partials/disconnects/retries. They care about predictable unit economics during PoC (likely 4–6 weeks), but they're sensitive to being charged for noisy mobile/connectivity issues.

Can we do:
- Standard Q3 rate card pricing for baseline (see attached PDF).
- One-time 25k token "connectivity" credit for their PoC to safeguard against billing fallout from early mobile reconnections (applied if they hit >1% session interrupt rate in PoC).
- Internal note: confirm that our 90-second resume window is documented and supported by runtime (Vivek?) — also confirm whether idempotency token behavior is covered in SDK docs.

Marissa — any leeway on discounting the first 3 months on a 6-month commit? Stephanie — are we OK with issuing the small connectivity credit tied to a HubSpot milestone?

Thanks —
Jasmine
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-12T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Rate card + streaming metering questions

Jasmine / team — quick from billing:
- Discounting: for a 2M token/month commit we can offer a 7% commit discount baseline; if they commit 6 months we can tier to 10% after legal/finance sign-off. Marissa, please confirm if Sales wants to push to 12% for strategic logos.
- Connectivity credit: fine to issue a one-time 25k token credit for PoC (apply as an invoice credit tied to HubSpot deal NBH-2027-03-01). We'll mark credit expiration at 90 days.
- Metering semantics: Stephanie confirms the platform bills emitted tokens. For dedupe: the idempotency token must be provided by the client; otherwise dedupe is best-effort and node-local. We can add language in the SOW to require idempotency for retry-sensitive endpoints.

Vivek — can you confirm the 90-second resume window from runtime and any caveats (e.g., if model warming evicts KV cache earlier under memory pressure)?

Thanks —
Stephanie
Head of Billing Operations
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-12T16:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Rate card + streaming metering questions

Confirming runtime behavior:
- 90-second resume window is supported for streaming sessions where client reconnects with the same session id. We persist KV cache and the session metadata for up to 90s.
- Under peak memory pressure we may evict warm caches earlier; eviction is rare and we do try to honor resume windows for active PoC customers. We can add a clause: if eviction occurs due to sustained memory pressure we will notify and offer a one-time rerun credit (to be evaluated case-by-case).
- Idempotency header: SDKs include the idempotency header and examples in the docs; recommend customers use it for mobile-heavy clients with aggressive retry logic.

Happy to provide a short blurb we can include in the SOW and in the rate-card appendix.

-Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + streaming metering questions

Hi Sam — following up with our final summary and a proposed starter commercial for PoC.

Summary of metering and protections:
- Billing is per emitted token. Partial generations are billed only for tokens actually emitted.
- Retries that continue from the last emitted token will not be double-billed if you use the continuation token or idempotency header; otherwise dedupe is best-effort and may be node-local.
- We support a 90-second resume window for streaming sessions; KV cache persists for that window. In rare cases of memory-driven eviction we will coordinate and offer a one-time rerun credit.

Proposed PoC commercial:
- 2M token/month commit, 7% baseline commit discount for Q3 rate card pricing.
- One-time 25k token connectivity credit applied if PoC session-interrupt rate exceeds 1% (credit expires after 90 days).
- Legal SOW will include an appendix describing resume window behavior and idempotency guidance.

If you agree I can send an initial order form and SOW (DocuSign link) and Marissa will work the discount with Finance.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the scenarios.

Best,
Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
